targetText: Legislative reform and revolution are not different methods of historic development that can be picked out at the pleasure from the counter of history, just as one chooses hot or cold sausages. Legislative reform and revolution are different factors in the development of class society.
explanation: Luxemburg's iconic rejection of reformist choice: reform and revolution are not menu options for political activists; legislative reform operates within the boundaries of existing class society, whereas revolution creates a new social order.

targetText: That is why people who pronounce themselves in favour of the method of legislative reform in place and in contradistinction to the conquest of political power and social revolution, do not really choose a more tranquil, calmer and slower road to the same goal, but a different goal. Instead of taking a stand for the establishment of a new society they take a stand for surface modifications of the old society.
explanation: Exposing revisionism's true objective: substituting reform for revolution does not reach socialism slowly—it abandons socialism altogether in favor of managing and preserving capitalism.

targetText: The fate of democracy is bound up, we have seen, with the fate of the labour movement.
summary: Democracy survives and grows only as far as the labour movement is strong, not through the generosity of the bourgeoisie.
explanation: Luxemburg argues that bourgeois democracy is no steady upward progress. As the bourgeoisie turns reactionary out of fear of the working class, defending democratic rights becomes a task of the proletariat itself.
context: Her chapter on the conquest of political power asks whether democracy makes revolution unnecessary and concludes that it does not.
